SpaceX IPO occurred on June 12, 2026, marking the largest initial public offering in history with a target valuation of US$1.77 trillion.
SpaceX listed on the Nasdaq exchange under the ticker symbol SPCX with a subscription price of US$135 per share.
Elon Musk retained 82% to 85% of voting power post-IPO through Class B shares that carry ten votes per share.
SpaceX raised approximately US$86 billion from the offering, which included a greenshoe option of 83,333,333 shares.
The IPO raised capital to fund long-term ambitions including building orbital artificial intelligence infrastructure for the xAI subsidiary.
Nasdaq allowed SpaceX early inclusion in the Nasdaq-100 index just 15 trading days after the IPO due to a specific rule change.
SpaceX was ineligible for the S&P 500 index because it reported a net loss of US$4.94 billion in fiscal year 2025.
Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley served as lead underwriters for the deal with fees totaling less than 0.75% of the offering.
Anthropic signed a contract worth US$1.25 billion per month to purchase all compute capacity at the Colossus 1 data center.
Google signed a cloud computing agreement to pay US$920 million monthly for compute capacity to power its Gemini models.
Bloomberg reported that underwriters denied subscription orders from investors in Hong Kong and China due to regulatory risks.
SpaceX launched a US$20 billion bond issue ten days after listing to repay bridge loans and cover corporate expenses.
Analysts at underwriting banks issued uniformly bullish 12-month price targets ranging from US$190 to US$800 despite the stock falling below the IPO price.
Professor Aswath Damodaran modeled SpaceX's segments to arrive at an enterprise value of approximately US$1.3 trillion.
The IPO stock price reached a first-day close of US$161 per share, representing a 19% increase from the subscription price.
